title: ‘Our children are less cognitively capable,’ says neuroscientist who wants to cut screen use in schools

paragraphs.en: Jared Cooney Horvath is on a mission. In the wake of global campaigns for smartphone bans in schools and social media restrictions for under-16s, the neuroscientist wants to raise the alarm about educational technology in classrooms.
paragraphs.zh: 贾里德·库尼·霍瓦特（Jared Cooney Horvath）肩负着一项使命。在全球掀起学校禁手机运动和限制 16 岁以下青少年使用社交媒体的浪潮之际，这位神经科学家想要就课堂上的教育技术发出警报。

paragraphs.en: A former teacher, Horvath believes the use of screens and digital tools in schools is undermining how children learn and develop. “This might be one of the hardest truths our generation has to face,” he writes in his book, The Digital Delusion .
paragraphs.zh: 身为前教师的霍瓦特认为，学校中屏幕和数字工具的使用正在损害儿童学习和发展的方式。“这可能是我们这一代人必须面对的最艰难的真相之一，”他在其著作《数字错觉》（The Digital Delusion）中写道。

paragraphs.en: “Our children are less cognitively capable than we were at their age,” he says. “For nearly two centuries, the west experienced steady generational progress. Each new cohort of children grew up, on average, healthier, happier, and better educated than the last. Until now.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们的孩子在认知能力上不如我们当年同龄时的水平，”他说。“近两个世纪以来，西方经历着稳定的代际进步。每一代新的孩子长大后，平均都比上一代更健康、更快乐、受教育程度更高。直到现在。”

paragraphs.en: Starting around the year 2000, something changed. “Across the west, IQ scores began to fall – even as time spent in school kept rising,” writes Horvath. Scores in international tests started to drop. Why? “The answer lies in the meteoric rise of educational technology.”
paragraphs.zh: 大约从 2000 年开始，情况发生了变化。“在整个西方，智商分数开始下降——即便在校时间不断延长，”霍瓦特写道。国际测试的分数也开始下滑。为什么？“答案在于教育技术的飞速崛起。”

paragraphs.en: According to a recent Department for Education report, the UK educational technology – or edtech – market generated an annual turnover of about £6.5bn. In the US, Horvath says it is a $400bn (£295bn) mega-industry, woven into every aspect of schooling.
paragraphs.zh: 根据英国教育部最近的一份报告，英国教育技术（edtech）市场的年营业额约为 65 亿英镑。霍瓦特说，在美国，这是一个 4000 亿美元（2950 亿英镑）的超级产业，已渗透到学校教育的方方面面。

paragraphs.en: “We’ve been making some incredible strides on the screen-based childhood stuff which even two years ago, I did not think was going to happen as fast as it did,” he said. “But it’s not just about getting rid of screens for entertainment. It’s about reducing them as much as possible for academic learning as well if we want our kids to have deep transferrable knowledge in our heads.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们在‘屏幕化童年’的问题上取得了令人难以置信的进展，哪怕两年前，我也没想到它会发展得这么快，”他说。“但这不仅仅是让孩子远离娱乐用的屏幕。如果我们希望孩子们掌握深刻的、可迁移的知识，那么学术学习方面也要尽可能减少屏幕的使用。”

paragraphs.en: The uptake of laptops in schools – especially in the US where he lives – began in earnest in 2010-12, Horvath said, but it was when Covid hit a decade later that “every school had to pivot digital as a Band-Aid … rightly so. Better to have something than nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 霍瓦特说，学校开始大量配备笔记本电脑——尤其是在他居住的美国——始于 2010 至 2012 年，但直到十年后新冠疫情来袭，“每所学校才不得不把数字化当作创可贴……这也情有可原。总比什么都没有要好。”

paragraphs.en: “But when Covid finished you would assume they’d rip that Band-Aid off, but the vast majority of schools didn’t. They just stayed digital.” In the US 88% of school districts now had one-to-one computers, he said. In the UK, Covid had a similar impact.
paragraphs.zh: “但疫情结束后，你会以为他们会撕掉这块创可贴，然而绝大多数学校并没有这么做。他们只是继续维持数字化。”他说，如今美国 88% 的学区都实现了人手一台电脑。在英国，新冠疫情也产生了类似的影响。
